history.origins: Cap-It is a variation of Push, a Contract Rummy game contributed by Paul Welty. The Cap-It variant was described by Wayne Ostrowski. It modifies Push by eliminating partnerships, dealing 10 cards each round, and changing the fifth round contract.
timeline: Original Push game developed as Contract Rummy variant
Current: Played as gambling game with pot contributions
history.cultural: Played as a social gambling game where all players contribute to a pot. Winner of each round takes a share, overall winner takes remainder. Popular in casual gaming circles.
history.evolution: Cap-It evolved from Push by: (1) eliminating partnerships for individual play, (2) dealing 10 cards each round instead of increasing deals, (3) changing the fifth round contract to run of 3 + run of 7, (4) adding gambling element with pot.

setup.players: 4-6 players, each playing individually (no partnerships). For 4 players: 2 decks. For 5-6 players: 3 decks.
setup.deck: 4 players: 108 cards (2Ã—52-card packs + 4 jokers). 5-6 players: 162 cards (3Ã—52-card packs + 6 jokers). Jokers and 2s are wild. Cards rank A-K-Q-J-10-9-8-7-6-5-4-3-2 (Ace high or low in runs).
setup.dealing: All 5 rounds deal 10 cards to each player (unlike Push which increases). Remaining cards form stock. Turn up one card to start discard pile (cannot be wild - if 2 or joker, bury and turn up next).
setup.equipment: 2 or 3 standard 52-card packs with jokers, chips/money for pot, score sheet

rules.objective: Be the first to go out (play all cards) each round. Lowest cumulative penalty points after 5 rounds wins the pot.
rules.gameplay: 5 rounds total, all dealing 10 cards. Each round has specific contract for initial meld: Round 1: 2 sets of 3; Round 2: 1 set of 3 + 1 run of 4; Round 3: 2 runs of 4; Round 4: 3 sets of 3; Round 5: 1 run of 3 + 1 run of 7. Turn: Draw (take discard top OR push discard+stock card to left player and take next stock card), meld (must meet contract for first meld), discard. Sets: 3-4 cards same rank (max 4 since 2 decks, no duplicate suits in set). Runs: 3+ same suit sequence, Ace high or low (not both). Wild cards (2s/jokers) substitute any card. Can lay off on any meld after meeting contract. Can replace wild cards with natural cards from hand (wild must be used immediately in new meld). Go out by melding/discarding all cards.
keyRules: Must meet contract before any other melding
Draw: take discard OR push discard+stock to left and take next stock
Sets: 3-4 cards same rank, no duplicate suits
Runs: 3+ consecutive same suit, Ace high or low
Round 5 contract: run of 3 + run of 7 (different from Push)
Can replace wilds with naturals (wild must be reused immediately)
Lowest cumulative score after 5 rounds wins pot

strategy.basic: Focus on meeting the contract requirement first. Hold wild cards for flexibility. Watch what cards opponents are collecting.
strategy.intermediate: Plan ahead for upcoming contracts. Use the 'push' mechanic strategically - forcing cards on opponents can disrupt their plans. Replace wild cards when beneficial to free them for other melds.
strategy.advanced: Track discards and pushes to deduce opponent hands. Time your go-out to maximize opponent penalties. In gambling version, manage risk based on pot size and your position. Round 5's run of 7 is difficult - prepare early.
tips: Save wild cards for difficult contracts
The push mechanic can be used defensively to give opponents unwanted cards
Round 5's run of 7 requires early preparation
Replacing a wild card can enable a new meld
Going out quickly may be better than perfect melds
Watch opponent discards for clues about their contracts
